A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlowerDance and are fully readable, including equations, figures, tables and references. Both contain ten pages and end with references; neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original evaluations on FineDance and AIST++, a 40-participant user study, component ablations and qualitative motion-editing results.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original benchmark evaluations, user study, ablations and qualitative results, including Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same MeanFlow procedure, physical-consistency losses, BiMamba architecture, channel-level fusion and time-decayed soft-mask editing.

E1.justification: Both retain FineDance and AIST++ evaluations, the in-the-wild music user study and motion-editing demonstrations. No dataset, domain or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical benchmark and user-study comparator sets. Table 4 still compares MeanFlow with RectFlow and Diffusion; Table 5 retains the same component substitutions.

E3.justification: The reported test protocols, 1024-frame and 1200-frame outputs, metrics, sampling-step comparisons, and double-blind study with 40 participants and 40 music segments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Sampling-step, backbone, fusion and physical-constraint ablations in Tables 4–5 are unchanged, as are the Eastern Folk case study and soft-versus-hard-mask analysis in Figures 3–4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. Point-estimate and user-study reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–5 and the qualitative findings are retained. For example, FlowerDance's FineDance FIDk remains 29.73 and inference speed remains 2008 FPS; AIST++ FIDk remains 20.50.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same definitions, MeanFlow derivation, losses, masking rule and state-space equations, numbered 1–12. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about dance quality, generation efficiency, few-step sampling, non-autoregressive generation and interactive editing.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and applicability qualifications are unchanged, including discussions of one-step collapse, few-step jitter, Transformer extrapolation failures and hard-mask transition artifacts.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page URL after the abstract, providing an access pointer absent from v1. Both still promise code release upon acceptance; no implementation settings or confirmed code-release information are added.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and all 52 references are retained. Changed citation-page back-references for VoiceFlow and Matcha-TTS merely reflect text reflow.

P1.justification: v3 adds the project-page line, removes a stray space before a period in the abstract and updates the arXiv version/date text. The narrative and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Opening-page spacing and Figure 1 positioning change slightly, with text reflow across pages 1–3. Figure and table content and structure are unchanged; pages 4–8 render identically.

improvement.justification: The added project-page pointer offers a small convenience, while punctuation and layout edits have negligible effects on readability. Scientific explanations, evidence and conclusions are unchanged. Both retain the promise of code release upon acceptance, so the PDFs establish no meaningful improvement in reproducibility or overall paper quality.
